title: Space-constructible functions
statement: A function $S:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ is space constructible if $\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor+1\le S(n)$ for every natural number $n$, and there exist a positive natural number $c$ and a finite Boolean Turing machine that, on every Boolean input $x$, outputs the binary representation of $S(|x|)$ using at most $cS(|x|)$ work-tape cells.
hypotheses_covered: $S$ is a function from natural numbers to natural numbers
for every $n$, the logarithmic space bound is at most $S(n)$
there exists a finite Boolean Turing machine computing the binary representation of $S(|x|)$ on every Boolean input $x$
the machine uses at most $cS(|x|)$ cells of space
